G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd


Raghav Khanna  ·  Regional Head
On joining GLEUHR
Dear Raghav,
Welcome to GLEUHR. I am glad you have joined. I am writing this note to give you, in my own words, what I want from this role and what you can expect from me — separately from the formal KRA document you will also receive.
The role you have taken is one of the most important in the company. The brand is built one clinic at a time, and the difference between a branch that flourishes and one that quietly drifts is almost always the quality of leadership it gets. Manisha leads sales for the company. You lead the region. The five branches you own — and the five your peer owns — are the operating heart of GLEUHR. What happens in those branches every day is what the customer experiences as our brand. Nothing higher up matters if that experience is not consistent, warm, and clinically excellent. Holding that experience is your job.
I want to tell you how I think about this role. You are not a travelling auditor. You are not a head office presence that visits and judges. You are a player-coach. When you walk into a branch, your job is to leave it measurably better than you found it — and the BM you worked alongside should feel stronger after your visit, not smaller. Every Regional Head can choose between two styles: the one who walks in and finds things wrong to prove their value, or the one who walks in and builds capability so the branch holds the standard after they leave. I expect the second. The first is easy and the second is hard, and I am paying for the hard one.
Practically — you will spend twenty to twenty-two days a month in the branches, in cycles of five to six days each. Day one is audit and action plan together with the BM. Day two is training and the start of execution. Days three and four are execution alongside the team. You hand over to the BM only when execution is running smoothly without your interference — typically day five or day six. Then you move to the next branch. Over a month you will touch every branch in your region; over a quarter, every branch should have visibly improved on the metrics we agree. The BMs report to you. You report on sales and revenue to Manisha. You report on clinic operations to Saurabh. Both Manisha and Saurabh report to our Chief Business Officer, who reports to me. This is by design — sales discipline and operations discipline are different muscles, and the company is large enough now that they need different lines holding each.
Before you go into the field, you will spend seven to fourteen days at the Chandigarh branch — the length depends on how quickly you absorb the work. The training is built in two streams. First — Sales end-to-end. How leads come in, how the online appointments team converts a lead into a booked client, how that handoff reaches the branch, how the counsellor closes, follows up, upsells. Manisha owns this stream. Second — Operations. Reception, doctors, clinical protocols, therapists, housekeeping, hygiene, everything that happens inside the four walls of a branch. Saurabh owns this stream. There is a training tracker your trainers will fill for each module. You are signed off as ready for the field only when every module is complete and your trainers — Manisha and her team for sales, Saurabh and his team for operations, plus Jaspreet at Chandigarh and Arshpreet for compliance — agree you are ready. Not before. We do not put Regional Heads into the field half-trained. The damage they cause when they correct things they don't fully understand takes months to repair.
When training is complete, Manisha and I will meet you together to sign off and send you to the field. That is the moment I trust you with five branches and five BMs. From that point on, you carry the region.
Here is what you can expect from me. I will not micromanage you. Once we have signed off on your readiness, I trust you to make decisions in your region. I will not call a BM directly without telling you first. I will not undercut you in front of anyone. When you ask for a decision from me, I will respond within twenty-four hours, even if the answer is 'I am thinking about it.' If you tell me something is hard, I will believe you the first time. You start with my trust. You only lose it if you lie to me — once is enough.
Here is what I want from you in return. Be honest with me even when honesty is uncomfortable. Tell me a problem before I find it from somewhere else. Do not protect a BM who is failing — your loyalty is to the company, not to the people who happen to report to you on any given day. Do not have favourites among your BMs; do not let one branch become your inner circle. Adhere to leadership decisions seriously — if you disagree, raise it with me or with Manisha directly, but once a decision is locked, you are the person who carries it down. Own every problem inside your region, even when its cause sits elsewhere. Never use another team as the shield for a gap in yours.
I will meet you again at the end of training, with Manisha and Saurabh. Beyond that, the regular rhythm: a weekly thirty-minute call with Manisha on sales, a weekly thirty-minute call with Saurabh on operations, a monthly business review with the CBO, and a quarterly in-person review with the four of us. If something urgent comes up — a serious complaint, a regulatory issue, a key person leaving — message me directly. I will pick up. Outside that, the day-to-day partnership is between you and the two people who hold your two streams, and that is by design. The structure works best when the regional layer is genuinely empowered.
One last thing. I picked this moment to build the Regional Head structure because the company is moving from a stage where I could be in every branch myself to one where I cannot. That transition only works if the people I hand the branches to carry them with the same seriousness I would. I have hired you because I believe you can. The next ninety days will be the test — for you, for the model, and for the company. Walk into your first branch knowing that you are not stepping into a job. You are stepping into the architecture of how this brand will look five years from now.
See you in Chandigarh.

With respect, and with high expectations,

Urminder Singh
Founder & Managing Director  ·  Gleuhr Wellness Pvt Ltd


Handed over on Day 1 of joining. Accompanied by the KRA/KPI document and the training framework.
